pylons_vi: 2 tháp chữ A (Y ngược) màu trắng, cao 110 m trên mặt cầu (≈164 m toàn tháp): hai chân đứng trên bệ cọc, giao nhau ở ≈68 m rồi vươn thành hai bản song song có khe hẹp đến đỉnh tháp xuyên lỗ; dây văng đỏ hai mặt phẳng, dạng nửa rẻ quạt
pylons_en: 2 white 'A' (inverted-Y) pylons, 110 m above the deck (≈164 m overall): legs on a large pile cap meet at ≈68 m and continue as two slotted blades to a pierced crown; red semi-fan stays in two planes

model3d.notes: Cable-stayed unit 210 + 450 + 210 m (2nd-longest span in Viet Nam), steel–concrete composite girder (twin red steel edge girders under a concrete slab), two stay planes, deck 21.5 m (4 lanes). Navigation clearance 160 × 45 m (Báo Đầu tư / KTNN; 2019 brief: H 45 m, B ≥ 300 m, 10,000 t). Pylons P23/P24 per the official render: white 'chữ A' / inverted-Y towers, 110 m above the deck (press); the legs stand on square plinths on a chamfered pile cap (≈60 × 30 m, corners cut 9 m (G18 chamfer_m), 32 Ø2.5 m piles up to 116 m), pass outside the deck edges with a deck-level crossbeam under the girder, converge at ≈68 m above the deck and rise as two blades with a narrow slot to a capital at ≈98 m, topped by a pierced crown and spike. SGGP's 164 m is the whole tower from the cap (render: ≈152 m cap top to tip, deck ≈47 m above the water at the pylons). Red semi-fan stays (#c8262c with G14 vivid, so they read red rather than brick), ≈20 per side per plane (read from the render), anchored over ≈63–97 m. One auxiliary pier per back span ≈60 m from each unit end (render). Deck ≈41 m above the water at the unit ends, ≈47.2 m at the pylons, ≈49.5 m at mid-span (crest 8.5 m).

pylon_custom.description: Inverted Y / 'chữ A' across the bridge (official render): two straight legs on square plinths on a chamfered pile cap, z ±20 m at the cap, passing outside the 21.5 m deck at z ±14 with a 5 m deep crossbeam under the girder; they converge to ±2.1 m at ≈68 m above the deck (small link, the dark 'eye'), rise as two parallel blades with a ≈1.2 m slot to a capital at ≈98.5 m, and close into a pointed crown at 110 m (the real crown is pierced, with a spike). Stays anchor on both blades in two planes running to the deck edges.
